Definition: Whether government taxes, customs duties, and other revenue can be paid using the instant digital payment system, indicating integration of payment infrastructure with tax administration systems.
Comments: World Bank ISR for Benin Economic Governance for Service Delivery PforR reports that 86.01% of revenue from P2G payments was collected digitally as of 31-Dec-2023, demonstrating digital revenue collection is in active use ([World Bank ISR – Benin Economic Governance for Service Delivery PforR](https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/099092325063510323/pdf/P176763-2035557c-fe0f-4162-a072-04b417dfb137.pdf)).
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed with a second independent source. The World Bank ISR (Seq. 05427, DLI data) shows 86.01% of P2G revenue and 95% of VAT / 35-41% of property tax collected digitally by 31-Dec-2023/2024; a separate UNDP Benin digitisation report (2026) independently states that "90% of taxes and duties in Benin are paid via the digital channel". Value Code 3 (Yes) confirmed.

Definition: Whether an official government web portal or mobile application exists where taxpayers can file tax returns and pay taxes online with direct e-payment capability linked to instant payment system.
Comments: Benin’s Directorate General of Taxes (DGI) operates the “e-services.impots.bj” portal launched in 2017 and has continued adding online services; May 2024 reporting notes new online tax services for micro/small businesses and property owners and references the existing portal ([We are Tech Africa – Benin launches new online tax services](https://www.wearetech.africa/en/fils-uk/news/benin-launches-new-online-tax-services-for-businesses-and-property-owners)).
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed with a second independent source. IMF Staff Country Report (Dec 2024) corroborates that DGI's e-services tax portal (e-services.impots.bj), launched 2017, offers online declaration and payment with phased functionality additions for businesses and individuals. Value Code 4 (Yes) confirmed.

Definition: Whether the instant payment system enables or plans to enable instant payments across national borders to other countries or regional payment systems, supporting remittances, trade, and regional integration.
Comments: PI‑SPI is a WAEMU-wide interoperable instant payment platform enabling transfers/payments across account types within the eight WAEMU countries (including Benin), implying regional (cross-border within WAEMU) functionality as participants connect ([World Bank – Fast Payments: PI‑SPI](https://fastpayments.worldbank.org/node/595);[BCEAO press release – PI‑SPI participants at launch](https://www.bceao.int/fr/communique-presse/liste-des-participants-autorises-ouvrir-les-services-de-pi-spi-au-public-30-sept-2025)). Evidence collected does not confirm linkages beyond WAEMU or full cross-border corridors outside the union; thus scored as partially functional.
redteam_note: Comment wording may not match the score — re-read (needs judgement).
revision_notes: Confirmed with fresher evidence. PI-SPI (launched 30-Sep-2025) is a live, WAEMU-wide cross-border instant payment rail covering Benin and 7 other member states. However, BCEAO's 25-Jun-2026 communiqué shows only 80 institutions connected to the public service and a further 74 in real-world testing, with connection deadlines extended to 30-Sep-2026 (banks/e-money issuers) and 30-Jun-2027 (microfinance institutions). This confirms cross-border functionality exists but rollout is incomplete as of mid-2026, supporting "Partially functional" (4) rather than "Fully functional" (5).

Definition: Whether payment system operators or regulators regularly publish performance metrics and statistics on system usage, transaction volumes/values, participant numbers, uptime, and other operational indicators.
Comments: BCEAO publicly releases recurring statistical publications (e.g., Quarterly Statistical Bulletin) that include Benin monetary/financial tables and are published on BCEAO website ([BCEAO – Quarterly Statistical Bulletin 3Q2024 PDF](https://www.bceao.int/sites/default/files/2025-04/Quaterly%20Statistical%20Bulletin%20-%203Q2024.pdf)). However, this evidence is not specific to payment-system performance metrics (e.g., PI‑SPI/SICA/STAR uptime, speed, volumes) and is therefore treated as ad hoc for payment system performance reporting.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Revised upward. Found BCEAO's explicitly named "Tableau de bord annuel de la monétique régionale dans l'UEMOA" (annual regional card-payment scorecard, 2023 edition) plus a periodic (roughly biennial) "Rapport sur les infrastructures de marchés financiers, les moyens et les services de paiement" (latest covering 2022-2023, published Jun-2025), together with a live PI-SPI "chiffres clés" statistics page. This is more systematic and regular than ad hoc, supporting Annual (3). Note these are UEMOA-wide rather than Benin-specific publications; no evidence found of monthly/quarterly payment-system-specific reporting.

Definition: Percentage of the adult population (15+ years) who have made at least one digital payment transaction through the instant payment system in the past 90 days, indicating active usage rather than just account ownership.
Comments: IMF reports that as of 2022 the number of active mobile money accounts per 1,000 adults reached 1,104 (over one active account per adult), indicating very high usage penetration (acknowledging that some individuals can hold multiple accounts) ([IMF eLibrary – Benin Digital Transformation to Foster Inclusive Growth](https://www.elibrary.imf.org/view/journals/002/2024/339/article-A002-en.xml)). Based on this evidence, score in the 70–89% bracket rather than >89% (to avoid over-interpreting accounts-per-adult as unique users).
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Retained but flagged for human review. GSMA's 2025 Benin digital economy report (2023 data) finds 11.2m active mobile money accounts, equal to 89% of total population and ~140% of the adult population — indicating widespread multiple-account holding. IMF/FRED data show 1,331 active accounts per 1,000 adults in 2024. These are account-based, not unique-user, measures, so the true unique-adult active-usage share cannot be confidently pinned to one band — it is at least 70-89% and plausibly higher (>89%). Value Code 4 kept as a conservative estimate; recommend human review with Global Findex 2025 unique-respondent data (not yet analysed here) to confirm whether band 5 is warranted.

Definition: Percentage of government payments (G2P disbursements including salaries, pensions, social transfers) made through instant digital payment system rather than cash or check, reflecting government adoption and modernization.
Comments: World Bank ISR for Benin Economic Governance for Service Delivery PforR reports (31-Dec-2023) that 86.01% of revenue from P2G payments was collected digitally, implying a large share of government revenue collection flows digitized ([World Bank ISR – Benin Economic Governance for Service Delivery PforR](https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/099092325063510323/pdf/P176763-2035557c-fe0f-4162-a072-04b417dfb137.pdf)). However, the same ISR indicates 0% of social program beneficiaries receiving digital G2P payments, so digitization is high for revenue but not for transfers; score as 50–69% overall government payment digitization.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Revised down — the original score conflated P2G (tax) digitisation with G2P disbursement. On fetching the full WB ISR DLI table, the actual G2P indicator states "(i) 0 percent of beneficiaries of the social programs [back-to-school bonuses, scholarships, pensions, and other social transfers] receive digital G2P payments" as of 31-Dec-2023, against a 2028 target of 95%; the 86.01% figure cited in the original comment refers only to P2G revenue collection, not government disbursements. Benin's Treasury confirms civil-service salaries and larger pensions are paid by ordinary bank transfer (bancarisation) and smaller pensions via mobile money, but no aggregate percentage of total G2P value digitised through an instant/digital payment system was found. Given the explicit 0% figure for social-programme G2P in the World Bank's own tracked indicator and the absence of a reliable all-in G2P percentage, revised to 1 (<20%); flagged for human review given ambiguity over whether ordinary bank transfer of salaries/pensions should count as an "instant digital payment system" for this variable's scope.
